arw_wide_country.accept_text:
The High Moor to the north, the low country south-east of the Pointe, and the gap in the wall to the south-west. Walk all three and do not ride.

I am not asking you to find anything. I am asking you to find out how long it takes, because every man I have lost up here was lost to thinking he could get somewhere before dark.

arw_witherbark_hollow.description:
There are Witherbark in a fold of ground on the far north-east side of the moor, and Scout Hollowfoot's report on them is one line long: they were here first and they are not going anywhere.

What has changed is that they have started coming out, which they did not do for the first eighteen months, and a troll village that changes its habits is a village that has had something happen to it.
arw_witherbark_hollow.accept_text:
I want to know what changed and I am not going to find out by asking, because the last two people who tried are part of the reason I am asking you.

Go in far enough that they commit to defending it. What they defend hardest tells you what they are worried about, and that is the report I actually need.

Witherbark Hollow is in the north-east corner of this country, the far side of the High Moor from the Pointe.

arw_what_veska_hears.accept_text:
Charms, and I want them lifted where they lie so I can see which way each one faced. Do not go for the harbinger. She is not the question.

The question is why a village would spend a year listening to itself.

The charms hang in Witherbark Hollow, north-east across the moor, and the shadowcasters carry the rest.
arw_what_veska_hears.turn_in_text:
All of them facing in. Every one.

They are not watching the moor. They are watching something that is already inside the hollow with them, and they have been doing it since about the time we arrived. I am going to need to think about whether those two facts are related.

arw_stro_the_claimant.accept_text:
He has a duelling sword and a court to use it in, except there is no court, there are nine bandits and a woman reading in the rain.

He is the one giving the orders that put bodies on my road. Everything else in that keep is furniture. Go and finish it.

Stromgarde Keep is south-west of the Pointe. You can see the towers from the road.

arc_the_bound.accept_text:
Cores. They have a stone at the centre and it is not the same stone as the rest of them - it is ring stone, off the circles, and that is a fact I would like five of rather than one.

And go back to the fourth ring afterwards - the one east of here, below Hammerfall. Three of those circles are quiet. The fourth is not, and I want you to have the cores in your hand when you stand in it.
arc_the_bound.turn_in_text:
Ring stone. All of them. They are made OF the circles - somebody took the monuments apart to make the guards that stand around the monuments.

That is a closed loop and I do not like it. It means whoever did it was not protecting the rings. They were feeding them.

arc_witherbark_village.description:
Deathguard Olen watches Hammerfall's gate from the Forsaken Quarter. Everything that has come through it in two years has been kobold, ogre, or a man with a very good reason.

Since the spring it has also been Witherbark, in numbers, from a village up the basin that had been keeping to itself since before the hold was built.
arc_witherbark_village.accept_text:
They were quiet for two years and now they are not, and nobody in this hold can tell me what changed.

I am not interested in why today. Today I am interested in fewer of them arriving at my gate at four in the morning. Go up the basin and make that happen, and then we can both be curious at a reasonable hour.

Witherbark Village is in the basin south-west of Hammerfall, on the far side of the Ring Road.

arc_the_hall.accept_text:
Krakk first - he is in the long hall and he is the one the rest of them watch. Then Hal'dun, who is the hold chief and who will not come out from behind the ring wall for anything.

I am not sending the garrison. A garrison takes the hold and then has to hold the hold. You go in, you end the two of them, and the rest of it stops being a problem without Hammerfall acquiring a second place to defend.

Boulderfist Hall is west of Hammerfall, clear across the Ring Road, at the far end of the highlands.

arc_dry_the_shift.accept_text:
I have watched a gate for two years and the thing I have learned is that people do not keep doing a job for no reason. They keep doing it because stopping is worse.

Bring me the whistle. I want to hold the object that nine hundred creatures have been obeying since before we got here.

The mine is Drywhisker Deeps, in the gorge south-east of Hammerfall.

arc_dry_the_brood.accept_text:
Shells and a look at the sump. I want the shells because a shell tells you the temperature it was laid at, and I want the sump because the sump is where the heat is coming from.

The Pick-Mother will be between you and both. I am sorry about that and I am going to ask you to do it anyway.

Drywhisker Deeps, in the gorge south-east of Hammerfall. The warm gallery is past the diggings.

arc_dry_below.accept_text:
I am not going to dress this up. Three of my people have been down to the sump and one came back, and what he said when he got here was that the water is not the bottom.

Go down. End it. And bring up whatever they were leaving on the floor down there, because they were leaving things on the floor, and a creature that leaves things on a floor is not mining any more.

Drywhisker Deeps again, south-east of Hammerfall, and this time all the way to the bottom of it.
arc_dry_below.turn_in_text:
Offerings. Arranged, and arranged is a word I have been avoiding since the Envoy first used it about the pearls in the mere.

That is Drywhisker finished and it is not Arathi finished. Rest. Eat something. Then go east, and when you get to the coast find a bosun called Tidewright and tell him Hammerfall sent you.
arc_dry_below.description:
Overlord Gath'rok has the prospector's seam report, the Deathguard's whistle and the apothecary's shell temperatures on the same table, and the them say one thing.

The kobolds of Drywhisker walked past a decade of iron, every day, for three years, to keep digging toward something below the sump. They found it. Nothing that has come up out of that mine since is behaving like a kobold.

are_six_wrecks.accept_text:
The flats, at low water, and do not be clever about the timing. The water comes back across the Spindrift faster than a person walks and I have watched it happen to somebody.

Every hull has a manifest tin bolted inside the stern post. Bring me what you can reach. I want to know what these ships were carrying, because this many wrecks on one archipelago is not weather.

There is a hull here on the Wrackline Shore, more out east at Bothy Rock, and one back toward Saltspur Landing, north-west of my camp.
are_six_wrecks.turn_in_text:
Tins, manifests, and three of them are the same cargo consigned to the same buyer.

These ships were not blown onto these rocks. They were coming here. Somebody was running a route into this archipelago and the route ate them.

are_they_are_holding.accept_text:
Watch orders, off three different islands. I want to see whether the same hand wrote them.

If it is three captains improvising, they are squatters and we can wait them out. If it is one hand, there is a plan, and a plan has an object.

Start with Gallowmast Isle, east across the flats from the Landing. The other two crews will find you.

Start with Gallowmast Isle, east across the flats from the Landing. The other two crews will find you. The Wrackline bosuns carry the orders. Their gunners will be between you and the bosuns.
are_they_are_holding.turn_in_text:
One hand. All of them.

So there is a plan and somebody is running it from inside that cave, and the object of it is on this archipelago somewhere. We are not the ones who turned up uninvited. We are the ones who turned up second.

arw_hold_the_road.turn_in_text:
All of them, and the adders, which nobody asked you for and everybody will thank you for.

The road will stay quiet for about nine days. I have measured it. That is not cynicism, that is a supply schedule.
arw_hold_the_road.accept_text:
You will not find a camp to burn. They do not have one on the road - they come down off the high ground, take what is loose, and go back up.

So you do it the slow way. Walk the road, and every time one of them comes down off the grass, make it the last time. That should get the message to whoever is counting on the other end.

And the moor adders. They lie on the warm road stone and bite whoever is walking it. Kill those too.

arw_the_gap.turn_in_text:
Slips and all of them agree with my book.

Eighteen months I have been doing this and it turns out I have been doing it correctly. I did not expect that to feel like anything. It does.
arw_the_gap.accept_text:
They cross at night and they cross in threes, and every one of them is carrying a slip with a number on it.

I want those slips. Not because I think they will tell me anything - because I have been counting for eighteen months and I would like, just once, to see somebody else's count.

arw_adder_season.accept_text:
Glands and whatever bruiseweed you can pull on the way. The weed grows along the road cuts - you will walk past it whether you are looking or not.

And keep the bruiseweed. I need to see it, not take it off you. I am not robbing people who do me favours, that is the Syndicate's business model.
arw_adder_season.description:
Quartermaster Horg keeps Refuge Pointe supplied, and Orgrimmar sends him less than a third of what the garrison needs. The rest he has to make himself.

Antivenin is top of the list. Moor adders come up out of the grass onto warm road stone at dusk and the camp has had four bites this month.
arw_adder_season.turn_in_text:
That is the camp covered until the weather turns.

Four bites this month and nobody died, because there was antivenin on the shelf each time. Keeping that shelf full is the whole of my work, and you have just done a week of it.

arw_the_overseer.turn_in_text:
Leaves and the house in uproar. Good.

The farmers get to keep farming either way, which was never going to change and was never the point. The point is that somebody in Alterac now has to explain a gap in the accounts. Let them.
arw_the_overseer.accept_text:
Get inside the house and be seen doing it. Take leaves out of whatever is on that desk - any three - and leave the rest on the floor.

They will move everything within a week and moving a ledger is when a ledger gets lost. I have waited a month for one page. I can wait a week for the rest of it to fall out of a cart.

arc_the_refuge_road.turn_in_text:
Maulers and the stone ones, and the road is a road again for about a fortnight.

I am not going to say I told them so. I am going to carry this report myself and put it in the Overlord's hand and stand there while he reads it.

arc_the_mere.accept_text:
Bladders, intact, and intact is the word that matters - they rupture if you are careless and what is inside them is the entire sample.

I am not asking you to be brave. I am asking you to be slow. Bravery has cost me two couriers and no data.

arc_the_silt_mother.accept_text:
Pearls off the bed and a good look at what is in the middle.

Freshwater pearls. In a mere. Something down there is making them and making them in rows, and I would like very much to know whether the rows mean anything or whether I am a man who has been alone with a pond for too long.

are_the_beachhead.accept_text:
The cutters come along the tideline at low water, which is the only time the flats are ground at all. Four hours a day, and nobody agrees which four.

Be on the shore when they are. Those, and the tidecrawlers that come up with them, and we get to keep calling this a landing instead of a mistake.

are_the_hermit.accept_text:
The petrels have the lee side. That was my side. I had it for two years and then there were more of them than there were of me, which is how most things end.

And bring me the down. Bundles. It is for a mattress. I am fifty-eight years old and I have been sleeping on a folded sail since before any of you got here.

And there is a reefmaw in the shallows under the rock. I would sleep better without it.

are_the_tidewrack.accept_text:
It grows them back. That is the thing about Brinemaw that everyone gets wrong - they think the teeth on the tideline mean something died.

Barbed ones and the animal itself. I need that sump clear and I need it clear before the weather turns, and I am not going to be precious about how.

The barbed ones are reefmaws. Kill them, and then Brinemaw.
are_the_tidewrack.turn_in_text:
Teeth, all barbed, and no animal grows a barbed tooth to eat with.

I am going to build a boat in there and I am going to try not to think about what that means. Shipwrights are very good at not thinking about the bottom.

are_wrack_drowned.turn_in_text:
Keepsakes an' t'ree of dem I can name.

Dey went out to look for people. Dat is all dey did wrong. Go an' rest, an' den come back, because dere is one more watch on dis coast dat nobody relieved an' it is older dan dis one by a long way.

arw_stro_the_claim.accept_text:
Get inside the outer ward and bring me their writs. They post them. On walls. In a keep nobody else lives in.

I want them for the archive and I want them because a forgery that good is a historical document in its own right, and in two hundred years somebody is going to believe it.

are_a_hull_that_floats.accept_text:
Ten of sound timber and fittings - bronze, off the rails and the cleats, and bronze because three years of salt has not touched it and iron is a brown stain.

Keep the timber. I need to see the grade before I plan around it. If it is all rot I would rather know now than halfway through a keel.

The timber is driftwood - cut it from the stumps and hulls out on the flats. Tidecrawlers nest in the wrecks, so clear those first.

arw_the_crags.accept_text:
Get up into the crags and come back able to tell me how many. Not an impression - a number, or the closest thing to one you can stand behind.

Kill what comes at you on the way. That is not the task, that is the weather.

The ones on the slopes are Boulderfist brutes. Count them, and kill the ones that see you.

arw_the_pit_chief.accept_text:
He counts out loud. Our scouts have heard him from outside the cave mouth.

The number he shouts is much higher than the number of ogres in that hold, and the difference is people off my road. Go down there and make the counting stop.

His name is Gor'mok. He is at the bottom of the Boulder'gor cave, in the pit.

arw_stro_the_gate.accept_text:
There is one way in and it is through him. I have had two scouts look at that wall and both came back with the same word, which was 'no'.

So go through the gate. Take the ward with it - the watch on that outer yard is thick and you will not get a second approach once they know you can get in.

Syndicate watchmen and footpads hold the outer yard. The man on the gate is called Grevan.

arw_stro_the_chapel.accept_text:
I want her book. Not her - her book, and if there is a way to come back with the one and not the other I would take it, and there will not be.

She is in a roofless room reading to nobody in a keep full of thieves, and whatever else that is, it is the only honest thing left in that building.

The Syndicate call her Sister Mollis.

arc_the_answer.accept_text:
Go and look at the North Shelf circle. The one closest to their hold.

I want to know how much of it is still standing. Not an estimate - I want somebody who has walked the ring and counted what is left, because if there is enough of it left then this is still a conversation, and if there is not then it stopped being one before I ever arrived.

Boulderfist maulers and shamans hold the ground round that circle. You will have to go through them to walk it.

are_the_ledger_keeper.accept_text:
Everything they have taken off six ships went across his shelf and into his book.

I want that book more than I want him, and I am aware I am going to get both. Bring it out dry. He keeps it high up for a reason and the reason is the only thing in that cave with any sense in it.

His name is Ashkin. The crew call him the Ledger-Keeper.

are_the_barrow_warden.accept_text:
You go in now. I already told you what dey are an' I not goin' to pretend dis is somet'ing else.

De warden on de stair first. Everyt'ing below it is holdin' a line dat warden is holdin' de top of, an' until dat shield come down, de rest of dem not goin' to even see you properly.

De ones behind it be Arathor revenants. Put dem down after.

arc_good_growing.accept_text:
Liferoot in the wet ground down the middle, kingsblood up where it is dry. Pull both and keep both - I want to see what the basin gives, not take it off you.

And the highland elk. I am sorry about the elk. They have found the liferoot too and there is not enough of it for both of us this year.
